links.title: Chapter 20 - Sending Emails, Texts, and Push Notifications, Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd Ed
links.why: The course textbook's own chapter, free online: the Gmail API with EZGmail, SMS email gateways, ntfy push notifications and the three practice programs.

links.title: email.message: Representing an email message
links.why: The standard library's EmailMessage: set headers, set_content, add_attachment and iter_attachments, all of which run offline.

links.title: smtplib — SMTP protocol client
links.why: How send_message() takes the recipients from To, Cc and Bcc and never transmits the Bcc field.

links.title: email.utils: Miscellaneous utilities
links.why: parseaddr, getaddresses and formataddr: taking a sender such as 'Al Sweigart <al@inventwithpython.com>' apart.

links.title: urllib.request — Extensible library for opening URLs
links.why: The Request object: data makes a POST, headers are a dictionary, and get_method() tells which, all without sending anything.

links.title: urllib.parse — Parse URLs into components
links.why: urlsplit, parse_qs and urlencode: the query string of a poll address such as /json?poll=1&since=10m.

links.title: json — JSON encoder and decoder
links.why: json.loads and the JSONDecodeError raised for text that holds more than one document.

links.title: email.header: Internationalized headers
links.why: Header and its encode method, which make an RFC 2047 encoded word for a title with letters outside ASCII.

links.title: hmac — Keyed-Hashing for Message Authentication
links.why: compare_digest, the constant-time comparison used for the password of the command-by-mail program.

links.title: secrets — Generate secure random numbers for managing secrets
links.why: token_urlsafe and choice: the right source for the random part of a secret topic name.

links.title: html.parser — Simple HTML and XHTML parser
links.why: The standard library's HTMLParser, enough to find links whose text says unsubscribe.

links.title: Sending messages - ntfy
links.why: Publishing: headers and their aliases, priority names, tags, and the limitations (4,096 bytes, 250 messages a day on ntfy.sh).

links.title: Using the API - ntfy
links.why: Subscribing: the JSON stream, poll=1, the values of since and every field of a message.

links.title: IMAP, POP, and SMTP | Gmail | Google for Developers
links.why: Gmail's own statement on the standard protocols: server names, ports and OAuth 2.0.

links.title: Transition from less secure apps to OAuth | Sync data | Google Workspace Help
links.why: The date, 14 March 2025, from which a password no longer works for IMAP and SMTP with Gmail.

links.title: Refine searches in Gmail - Computer - Gmail Help
links.why: The operators that ezgmail.search() accepts, such as from:, subject:, label: and has:attachment.

links.title: PEP 594 – Removing dead batteries from the standard library
links.why: Why smtpd, the standard library's test SMTP server, is gone from Python 3.12.

_note: Every url was opened with an HTTP fetch and its content read on the date in 'checked'; titles are those of the pages. The Python documentation pages served on that date were headed Python 3.14.8, while every behaviour was executed under 3.14.4. No video or discussion thread is listed: none was opened and read.
